name: FOG battle threads

card.summary: Themed forum threads that put two faces side by side and ask members to vote on which one "fogs" (out-looks) the other, giving users a shared reference for what facial features read as strongest.
card.note: Opinion polls among forum members; thread votes are not a validated measure of attractiveness.

quick.overview:
A FOG battle is a recurring thread format on looksmax.org in which the original poster shows two people, usually women or fictional characters, and asks readers to pick which one "fogs" the other. Fogging is the forum's term for visually overpowering someone with a stronger face or frame.

The payoff for appearance-minded members is comparative: by arguing over why one face wins, users spell out the traits they consider decisive, such as bone structure, lower third, hair volume, height and frame, and use that vocabulary when judging their own look. The threads are informal polls; no research tests their rankings.
quick.how: Threads are usually themed: hair colour (blonde), region or phenotype labels (North Atlantid, Latina, Mediterranean), country matchups, a film or game cast, or mother versus daughter. The opening post may list each contender's strengths and weaknesses, or simply present two photos with a numbered choice, and replies vote and argue the case.
quick.risks: Threads rate real people's faces and bodies by label and often attract insulting banter, and members who post their own photos can receive harsh comments. Votes reflect the preferences of a self-selected forum audience.

lead: A FOG battle (also written "fog battle" or "fog off") is a themed comparison thread on looksmax.org in which two faces are presented and members vote on which one "fogs" the other. The term comes from the forum's use of fogging and mogging for out-competing someone visually; Wikipedia describes mogging as slang from incel and manosphere communities for asserting dominance over someone through appearance [10].

Titles show the range of formats: "Fog Battle of the Unfoggables" between two well-known models [2], matchups by hair colour [15], country-versus-country "apex pheno" threads [8][9][12], regional groupings such as Latina or Mestiza [6][7], and lighter themes such as video-game characters [10] or a mother against her daughter [11]. Some threads rate members' own appearance, such as "org users as female true eve fog battle" [4].

For people working on how they look, the threads serve as a shared language. Posts name features like frame, height, phenotype, bone structure, hair volume and texture, and facial width-to-height ratio as the reasons a face wins or loses [2]. Members use those same terms when assessing which traits to work on. No published research has examined these threads or validated their outcomes.

angle.text: The threads give looksmaxxers concrete examples of which facial and body traits forum members rank highest. Participants use the feature-by-feature arguments as a reference when deciding what to improve in their own appearance.

paras: A typical post names a theme, shows two sets of photos and asks readers to choose. The simplest version lists two names and says to pick which one fogs, with members tagged to join in [1]. More elaborate posts give each contender a label such as "True Eve Face" or a regional phenotype, plus height, frame size and lists of strengths and weaknesses [2].

Another variant compares exaggerated opposites, for example an "Albino vs Vantablack" thread in which the reply chain digresses into the origin of the intensifier prefix "tera" (from the Greek for "monster") [3].

Region and phenotype threads compare countries or ethnic groupings under labels such as "apex pheno" [8][9][12], Latina and Mestiza matchups [6][7], and "Asians vs whites" [13]. Others cover hair colour with a face-only rule [15], a "full package" format that weighs more than the face [14], classic matchups between North Atlantid women [5], and pop-culture themes including Overwatch heroes [10]. A "mom vs daughter" thread frames inherited looks [11].

Replies mix votes with feature analysis and with jokes. In one thread a reply praises a contender as a "true Eve" that "fogs to oblivion" [1], while another thread's replies compare two models by frame, hair and height against a taller, wider-framed woman seen on social media [2]. The wider looksmaxxing vocabulary, including mogging and the PSL rating scale, is covered in the encyclopedia article on the movement, which notes that parts of PSL are described as pseudoscientific [10].

lore.intro: Members treat fog battles as both entertainment and a way to calibrate what a top-tier face looks like [2].

claims.claim: Specific features, such as frame, bones, height and lower third, decide who "fogs"
claims.believers: Posters list strengths and weaknesses such as frame, pheno, lower third, bones and height as the basis of a verdict [2].
claims.experts: No published research has tested these forum rankings; Wikipedia notes that parts of the related PSL scale are described as pseudoscientific [10].
